headline: Recommended placing the Parking Division within the Manchester Police Department; approved monthly financial reports for first three months of FY27.
summary: Finance staff reported that revenue for the first three months of FY27 was $1.3 million lower than a year ago. They linked part of the drop to delays entering items into a new accounting system, and said interest and rental income rose. A corrected unobligated amount for the Department of Public Works and Information Systems will be sent.
decisions: Approved the update on the City's Revolving Loan Fund.
Approved the receivables reports: accounts receivable over 90 days, aging report, and outstanding receivables.
Approved the City's monthly financial reports (unaudited) for the first three months of FY27.
Recommended that the ordinance placing the Parking Division within the Manchester Police Department pass and be enrolled, by a vote with the motion by Alderman Terrio and seconded by Alderman Goonan.

transcript:
## COMMITTEE ON ACCOUNTS, ENROLLMENT AND REVENUE ADMINISTRATION

November 17, 2026 at 5:00 PM

Chairman O’Neil called the meeting to order.

The Clerk called the roll.

Present: Aldermen O’Neil, Terrio, Goonan, Burkush, Vincent

Messrs.: K. LeBlanc, M. Bogardus

1. Update on the City's Revolving Loan Fund.

Kim LeBlanc, Financial Analyst II: Not much has changed since the committee last met. I have nothing to add to the report.

On motion of Alderman Terrio , duly seconded by Alderman Goonan , it was voted to approve.

2. Communication from Kim LeBlanc, Financial Analyst II, submitting Finance Department reports as follows:

- • Accounts Receivable over 90 days
- • Aging Report
- • Outstanding Receivables

K. LeBlanc: The amount has increased a little since we last met. We are working through some bugs with MUNIS, so some payments have been delayed getting into the system. We will get that rectified.

On motion of Alderman Vincent , duly seconded by Alderman Burkush , it was voted to approve.

3. Communication from Sharon Wickens, Finance Officer, submitting the City's Monthly Financial Reports (unaudited) for the first three months of FY27.

Michelle Bogardus, Deputy Finance Officer: Attached are the reports for the first three months of fiscal year 2027. As far as expenditures, the average unobligated balance percentage after three months should be 75% as a benchmark. All departments are within 10% of this benchmark, with the exception of the Department of Public Works and Information Systems. There's an error here. When it talks about the unobligated amount, it should read the unobligated amount after three months is $148.1 million for FY 27 and $143.2 million for FY 26. Health insurance costs are tracking through on November 17, 2026 COMMITTEE ON ACCOUNTS, ENROLLMENT AND REVENUE ADMINISTRATION

budget through September. And a comparison of retirements show that for 2027 $450,000 and for 2026, approximately $313,000. And contingency has remained unchanged at $200,000. On the revenue side for the first three months of fiscal year 2027, they are $1.3 million lower than a year ago. Auto registrations are a bit lower than the same time period. I believe that this may be a factor of some of the things getting entered into the new accounting system, delayed. School chargebacks are $1 million lower in FY 27, but that's basically due to timing, and Public Works and the Parking Division both have chargebacks that are delayed. Offsetting these decreases are interest incomes coming in $213,000 higher than last year and rentals and leases $272,000 higher.

Chairman O’ Neil: Can you repeat the number that you wanted to make sure was correct?

M. Bogardus: It should read $148.1 million for FY27 and $143.2 million for FY26. I can send a corrected letter.

On motion of Alderman Goonan , duly seconded by Alderman Burkush , it was voted to approve.

4. Ordinance Amendment:

“Amending Chapter 70: Motor Vehicles and Traffic of the Code of Ordinances of the City of Manchester by amending Section 70.44 Division Established hereby placing the Parking Division within the Manchester Police Department.”

On motion of Alderman Terrio , duly seconded by Alderman Goonan , it was voted that the Ordinance Amendment ought to pass and be Enrolled.

There being no further business, on motion of Alderman Terrio , duly seconded by

Alderman Vincent , it was voted to adjourn.

A True Record. Attest.

Clerk of Committee
